rows.reason: The host watchdog knows a turn stalled but settles it with {ok:false,text} only. The active coordinator/runtime converts that result to provider_error, losing the host cause; room setup-finally has the same loss.

originEvidence.detail: Watchdog settles direct follow-up with no stalled flag.
HostTurnResult has no stalled field.
Every !result.ok without cards/cap becomes provider_error.
Runtime.end likewise maps failure to provider_error.
Room finally records only ok/text, even when roomOutcome is stalled.
hostTurnResult can still return cards after a failed result.

rows.scenario: A coordinator-owned direct turn, or a room turn stalled during setup before a provider result, reaches the host watchdog. The watchdog stops it for inactivity and resolves the pending host outcome with ok:false. RuntimeCoordinator.run/end receives no cause and persists outcome:'provider_error' instead of 'stalled'; if resumable cards remain, hostTurnResult can instead park a turn already declared stopped.
upstreamEvidence: files/3325.json: stalled flag through HostTurnResult/EndResult, watchdog/room propagation, stalled outcome mapping, stopCards on stalled result
rows.scope: Useful cause-preservation fix across direct and room coordination. Origin's own runtime watchdog already has native stalled paths; patch only the host-watchdog settlement gap.
compatibilityGates: Preserve Origin direct-turn generation/resource ownership, retired-provider guards, setup-stall latching, computer parks and cap continuation behavior.
A stall must close its owned pending cards without cancelling another generation's cards; stopped/cancelled/provider-error outcomes must remain distinct.
Future isolated cases must include direct, room setup, late provider completion and owned cards; no fixture was run here.
rows.title: Record a turn the stall watchdog stopped as stalled, not as a provider error

rows.reason: Origin's strict chat schema compiler does not register Google's x-google-enum-descriptions annotation. A valid tool containing it is rejected during mount rather than offered to chat-completion models.

originEvidence.detail: Ajv compiler defaults to strict and registers formats only before compile at line 25.
Every mounted tool's original schema goes through compileToolSchema.
Schema error skips an optional server's staged tools, or throws for a required mount.

rows.scenario: A remote MCP tool advertises {type:'object',properties:{mode:{type:'string',enum:['a','b'],'x-google-enum-descriptions':['A','B']}}. Strict Ajv sees an unregistered keyword, compileToolSchema throws the generic validation error, and mountChatTools removes that optional server's tools for the turn. The annotation supplies descriptions rather than an extra input constraint.
upstreamEvidence: files/3299.json: register keyword with schemaType:'array'; chat tool test preserves enum validation
rows.scope: Small useful compatibility adaptation on the strict chat mount. Origin's lenient remote-proxy validator uses strict:false and is not the same failure path.
compatibilityGates: Register only this known annotation type; retain strict rejection of unknown constraint keywords and actual enum/type checks.
Do not globally disable strict validation or drop input validation; keep draft-07/2020-12 isolation and no external reference fetching.
rows.title: Google's remote MCP servers mount in chat: accept the x-google-enum-descriptions annotation

rows.reason: Origin already bounds oversized stdio results and preserves valid shortened structuredContent, with optional spill files. It does not hold JSON in memory or offer query_result. The PR adds queryable retained data, not a missing result-size safety boundary.

originEvidence.detail: Default result budget is 8000 characters.
trimCallResult divides the budget, optionally spills full text, and trims text at line 165.
Trims structuredContent as well.
Structural array trimming already exists.

upstreamEvidence: files/3300.json: mcp-shape.ts ResultStore/JMESPath query_result, mcp-gate injection, gateQueryTools preallow, jmespath dependencies
rows.scope: Useful for large JSON queries when repeated narrower upstream calls are expensive or impossible. Can be adapted independently of upstream chat-app observation; plain text can retain the current cut/spill behavior.
compatibilityGates: Keep query results budgeted, cap retention to the upstream 64 MB/session bound or stricter, and evict/clean per gate session.
Reserve/collision-handle query_result, preserve actual Origin tool selection and guest confinement, and preallow only that gate's read-only held-result tool.
Held results contain potentially sensitive data; never persist or share them across sessions/accounts/threads; keep structuredContent from bypassing the result budget.
Review the new JMESPath dependencies and query CPU/memory limits; do not apply the #3363 app-only test before its owning feature exists.
rows.title: perf(mcp): shape an oversized tool result instead of cutting it blind
